findings.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:117 — `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without optional chaining; when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (handleNewBooking sets it to `null` when neither the event type nor organizer has one) or `[]`, this throws a TypeError and kills booking creation for Google Meet locations. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` and safely fell back to Cal Video.

[High/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:255 (updateEvent) — the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only evaluated when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the predicate compares against a falsy value and can never match; `selectedCalendar` is always `undefined`, and `calendar.events.update` is called with an undefined `calendarId` (missing-required-parameter failure) instead of the previous fallback to the destination calendar's externalId.

[High/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315 (deleteEvent) — same self-referential broken fallback: when `externalCalendarId` is not provided, `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` never matches, `calendarId` is `undefined`, and the Google delete call fails, orphaning events on the calendar after cancellation.

[High/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:150 — the condition is inverted: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` became `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. Organizations now get a `slug` only when team billing is enabled (previously the opposite), so non-team-billing deployments create orgs with no slug, and team-billing deployments set `slug` immediately, bypassing the `requestedSlug` verification flow. This change is also unrelated to the PR's purpose.

[High/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:~427 — the fallback credential is fetched via `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` without `include: { app: ... }` and without mapping `appName` (compare the EventManager DB fetch, which sets `appName: credentialFromDB.app.slug`). `getCalendar` resolves the service from `appName`, so it returns `undefined` and `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` is silently skipped — collective booking events are never deleted from other hosts' calendars, which is the exact scenario this PR targets.

[Medium/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~375 (createAllCalendarEvents, no-credentialId branch) — `createEvent(c, event)` is called without `destination.externalId`, so `result.externalId` is `undefined` and the stored booking reference has no `externalCalendarId`; later update/delete for these bookings cannot locate the calendar (compounded by the broken Google Calendar fallbacks).

[Medium/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~150 (createEvent) — when no destination entry matches the passed `credentialId` (e.g., legacy destination calendars stored without `credentialId`), the code silently falls back to `"primary"` instead of using the destination's `externalId` as before, creating events on the wrong calendar for all matching credentials.

[Medium/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1073 + packages/core/EventManager.ts:~340 — no deduplication of destination calendars: each member's `user.destinationCalendar` is pushed and an event is created per entry, so if the event type's calendar equals a member's destination (shared team calendar) or two members share one, the same credential/calendar is processed twice and duplicate events are created on the same calendar.

[Medium/bug] packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73, packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128/162, packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:~160 — these services still resolve the target calendar from only the first destination calendar; since EventManager now creates per host with each host's credential, non-first hosts' credentials are paired with the main host's `externalId`, causing 404s/wrong calendars — multi-host collective bookings are broken for Office 365, Lark, and CalDAV/Apple calendars.

[Medium/data] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1875 — only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` is connected to the booking (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`); the schema still stores a single destination calendar, so for collective bookings all other hosts' calendars are lost, and every flow that rebuilds the CalendarEvent from `booking.destinationCalendar` (reminders, cancel, confirm, editLocation, payment webhooks) only ever sees the first host.

[Medium/security] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~750 (loadUsers catch) — `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` is rethrown as `HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: error.message })`, leaking raw internal database error details (table/field/meta info) to API clients and misclassifying server-side DB errors as client errors.

[Medium/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~540 (updateAllCalendarEvents merge path) — when merging bookings (`newBookingId`), only the first old calendar reference is deleted (`booking.references.find(...)`), but bookings can now have multiple calendar references, so old events on the remaining calendars are orphaned.

[Medium/test_gap] apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts is the only test touched — there is no coverage for the new multi-destination behavior: per-credential calendar selection in Google `createEvent`, event creation across multiple hosts' calendars, multi-reference update, or cancel deleting from all calendar references.

[Low/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~505 (updateAllCalendarEvents) — if the reference's credential is neither in `calendarCredentials` nor found in the DB (or `app.slug` is missing), `credential` stays `undefined` and `updateEvent(undefined, ...)` is invoked, throwing inside `getCalendar` and failing all references via the catch handler; a guard is needed.

[Low/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:~445 — the recurring-event deletion block now sits inside the per-reference loop, so with multiple calendar references it executes once per reference and attempts to delete the same updated bookings' events multiple times (duplicate API calls/errors).
[Low/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~590 — `console.error(message)` was removed from the catch handler, so calendar update failures are now silently swallowed with no logging/observability.

[Low/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1073 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when the organizer/event type has no destination calendar (`null`), silently dropping team members' destination calendars for collective events.

[Low/performance] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~340-380 and ~495-540 — the new per-destination loops `await` sequentially, including a per-destination `prisma.credential.findUnique` round trip and event creation, so collective booking latency grows linearly with host count; the credentialId path could be parallelized like the no-credentialId branch already is.

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the diff introduces `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then unconditionally reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` in the Google Meet fallback check. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]`, destructuring yields `undefined`, so `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a TypeError. The diff also shows `handleNewBooking.ts` can set `destinationCalendar` to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, making this crash path verifiable from the changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:255 (updateEvent) — the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only evaluated when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the predicate compares against a falsy value and can never match; `selectedCalendar` is always `undefined`, and `calendar.events.update` is called with an undefined `calendarId` (missing-required-parameter failure) instead of the previous fallback to the destination calendar's externalId.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is now computed as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When the ternary’s else branch runs, `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the condition failed), so the `.find()` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` against a falsy value (typically `undefined`/`null`) and will not match a real calendar externalId. This breaks the prior behavior (`: event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) and makes `selectedCalendar` effectively always `undefined` in the fallback path, so the update will not target the intended destination calendar (and may pass an undefined calendarId depending on the unchanged call site).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:315 (deleteEvent) — same self-referential broken fallback: when `externalCalendarId` is not provided, `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` never matches, `calendarId` is `undefined`, and the Google delete call fails, orphaning events on the calendar after cancellation.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, deleteEvent now computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is not provided (undefined/null), the `.find()` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined`), which will not match normal destination calendars, so `calendarId` becomes undefined. This breaks selecting the correct calendar for deletion and can cause the Google delete request to target an invalid/incorrect calendar (or rely on fallback behavior), potentially leaving the original event undeleted (orphaned).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `handleCancelBooking.ts` adding a DB fallback fetch via `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` without including `app` or mapping an `appName` field, and it is also true that the later call uses optional chaining (`calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`) so a missing calendar instance would be silently skipped. However, the finding’s key causal claim—“`getCalendar` resolves the service from `appName`, so it returns `undefined`”—cannot be verified from this PR diff (there is no change shown to `getCalendar`, nor its resolution logic). From the diff alone we can’t conclude that omitting `include: { app: ... }` will make `getCalendar` return `undefined`, or that collective events will “never” be deleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~375 (createAllCalendarEvents, no-credentialId branch) — `createEvent(c, event)` is called without `destination.externalId`, so `result.externalId` is `undefined` and the stored booking reference has no `externalCalendarId`; later update/delete for these bookings cannot locate the calendar (compounded by the broken Google Calendar fallbacks).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` `createAllCalendarEvents`, when iterating `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)`, the `else` branch for `!destination.credentialId` calls `createEvent(c, event)` without passing the destination’s `externalId`. After this diff, `createEvent` returns `{ externalId, credentialId }`, and downstream code in `EventManager` now uses `result.externalId` to populate `externalCalendarId` in booking references. Since `externalId` is never provided here, it will be `undefined`, so the stored reference lacks `externalCalendarId`, which can break later update/delete that rely on it. This is directly visible in the diff: the credentialId branch uses `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` but the no-credentialId branch does not.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~150 (createEvent) — when no destination entry matches the passed `credentialId` (e.g., legacy destination calendars stored without `credentialId`), the code silently falls back to `"primary"` instead of using the destination's `externalId` as before, creating events on the wrong calendar for all matching credentials.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `createEvent`, the calendarId is now chosen via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and then `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`. If destination calendar entries exist but don’t have a matching `credentialId` (e.g. legacy records with no `credentialId`), `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` and the code falls back to `"primary"`, whereas the previous behavior used `destinationCalendar.externalId` directly. This is verifiable from the diff and can route event creation to the wrong calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1073 + packages/core/EventManager.ts:~340 — no deduplication of destination calendars: each member's `user.destinationCalendar` is pushed and an event is created per entry, so if the event type's calendar equals a member's destination (shared team calendar) or two members share one, the same credential/calendar is processed twice and duplicate events are created on the same calendar.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `destinationCalendar` an array and, for COLLECTIVE team event types, appends each team member’s `user.destinationCalendar` into `evt.destinationCalendar` without any deduplication (handleNewBooking.ts: `teamDestinationCalendars.push(user.destinationCalendar)` and later `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). Event creation now iterates `event.destinationCalendar` and creates an event per entry (EventManager.ts `createAllCalendarEvents`: `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar) { ... createEvent(...) }`). Therefore, if the event type destination calendar equals a member’s destination calendar, or multiple members share the same destination calendar/credential, the same calendar can be processed multiple times, producing duplicate events on the same external calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73, packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128/162, packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:~160 — these services still resolve the target calendar from only the first destination calendar; since EventManager now creates per host with each host's credential, non-first hosts' credentials are paired with the main host's `externalId`, causing 404s/wrong calendars — multi-host collective bookings are broken for Office 365, Lark, and CalDAV/Apple calendars.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and updates `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` to create events per destination/credential (looping `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and calling `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`). However, Office365 (`packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`) and Lark (`packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`) still derive `calendarId` from only the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`). Likewise `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` (BaseCalendarService for CalDAV/iCal) filters calendars using only the first destination calendar’s `externalId`. Because the same `event` object (with an array of destination calendars) is reused for each credential, these services will keep using the main host’s `externalId` even when invoked with a different host’s credential, plausibly causing 404s or creating/updating in the wrong calendar for non-first hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1875 — only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` is connected to the booking (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`); the schema still stores a single destination calendar, so for collective bookings all other hosts' calendars are lost, and every flow that rebuilds the CalendarEvent from `booking.destinationCalendar` (reminders, cancel, confirm, editLocation, payment webhooks) only ever sees the first host.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and, for COLLECTIVE team events, explicitly appends other hosts’ destination calendars (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). However, when persisting the booking in `handleNewBooking.ts`, it only connects the first element: `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`. This means only one `destinationCalendar` is stored on the booking (consistent with all other code still reading `booking.destinationCalendar` as a single object and then wrapping it into a one-element array). As a result, any later flow that reconstructs a `CalendarEvent` from `booking.destinationCalendar` (e.g., reminders/payments/confirm/editLocation in this diff) cannot recover the additional hosts’ calendars, so those destination calendars are effectively lost from persisted state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~750 (loadUsers catch) — `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` is rethrown as `HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: error.message })`, leaking raw internal database error details (table/field/meta info) to API clients and misclassifying server-side DB errors as client errors.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts`, the new `loadUsers` function wraps Prisma access in a `try/catch` and explicitly converts `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` into `new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: error.message })`. Prisma known-request errors often contain internal DB details (e.g., constraint names/fields), and returning `error.message` to the client can leak that information. Also, mapping a server-side DB failure to HTTP 400 misclassifies it as a client error. This behavior is directly shown in the added catch block.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~540 (updateAllCalendarEvents merge path) — when merging bookings (`newBookingId`), only the first old calendar reference is deleted (`booking.references.find(...)`), but bookings can now have multiple calendar references, so old events on the remaining calendars are orphaned.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, `updateAllCalendarEvents` was updated to treat `calendarReference` as an array via `.filter(...)` and iterate all references for updates. However, in the merge path (`if (newBookingId)`), it still deletes only a single old calendar event using `booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))`, which will return only the first matching reference. Since the diff explicitly enables multiple calendar references, this leaves other old calendar events undeleted/orphaned on remaining calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts is the only test touched — there is no coverage for the new multi-destination behavior: per-credential calendar selection in Google `createEvent`, event creation across multiple hosts' calendars, multi-reference update, or cancel deleting from all calendar references.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new logic around `destinationCalendar` becoming an array and multi-destination handling (e.g., `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over `event.destinationCalendar`, `updateCalendarEventOnBooking` now processes multiple `_calendar` references, `handleCancelBooking` now deletes across multiple calendar references, and Google `createEvent` now selects a calendar by matching `credentialId`). The only test change in the diff is in `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts`, updating an expected payload field from `destinationCalendar: null` to `destinationCalendar: []`, with no added/updated tests covering the new multi-destination behaviors mentioned. This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap but not a direct functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:~445 — the recurring-event deletion block now sits inside the per-reference loop, so with multiple calendar references it executes once per reference and attempts to delete the same updated bookings' events multiple times (duplicate API calls/errors).

adjudication.rationale: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts the code changed from a single calendar reference (find) to multiple references (filter) and now iterates `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. The recurring-event deletion block (`if (bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && bookingToDelete.recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings) { ... for (const updBooking of updatedBookings) { ... calendar?.deleteEvent(...) } }`) is inside that per-reference loop. Since that block deletes events for *all* `updatedBookings` across *all* calendar credentials, executing it once per reference will duplicate the same deletions (and push duplicate promises into `apiDeletes`), causing repeated API calls and potential errors when trying to delete already-deleted events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~590 — `console.error(message)` was removed from the catch handler, so calendar update failures are now silently swallowed with no logging/observability.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` catch block, `console.error(message);` was indeed removed (see the hunk replacing it with just a `Promise.resolve(...)` of failure results). There is no new logging added in that catch path, so runtime observability is reduced. However, the failure is not fully “silently swallowed” because the function still returns explicit `{ success: false, ... }` results to the caller; this is primarily a logging/diagnostics regression rather than a verifiable functional correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1073 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op when the organizer/event type has no destination calendar (`null`), silently dropping team members' destination calendars for collective events.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is explicitly set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`... : null`). Immediately after, for collective team events, the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, the optional chain causes `push` to be skipped, so any collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently not added. This matches the finding: team members' destination calendars can be dropped when the organizer/event type has no destination calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~340-380 and ~495-540 — the new per-destination loops `await` sequentially, including a per-destination `prisma.credential.findUnique` round trip and event creation, so collective booking latency grows linearly with host count; the credentialId path could be parallelized like the no-credentialId branch already is.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` `createAllCalendarEvents`, the new `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` loop performs `await prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` and then `await createEvent(...)` inside the loop when `destination.credentialId` is set, which is inherently sequential across destinations. Similarly, in `updateCalendarEvents`, it iterates `for (const reference of calendarReference)` and may `await prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` inside the loop before calling `updateEvent(...)`. This makes total latency scale roughly linearly with the number of destination calendars/references. This is a valid performance/architecture concern grounded in the diff, but not a correctness defect.
